nodes.meaning: The bounded business meaning owned by the ontology-management runtime capability.
An owner-configured declaration of one ontology package and every path the runtime may read or execute.
An immutable content-addressed read model derived from one exact registration and current selected source bytes.
The unchanged structured result emitted by the ontology owner's declared validator.
An immutable content-addressed identity over one closed ontology registration, its selected source bytes, and the evidence derived from that exact state.
The exact ontology epoch currently named by an owner-controlled active registration; its bytes and identity are historical facts and cannot be rewritten.
A separate durable successor bundle constructed from observed current bytes and validation evidence, with no admission, acceptance, or activation authority.
A bounded comparison between an admitted registration identity and current selected bytes that records every changed, missing, ambiguous, or invalid input.
A repository-local append-only store of content-addressed epoch manifests, exact captured bytes, and validation receipts published atomically.
A fail-closed result that resolves one registration and declares whether a candidate can be constructed without granting mutation, admission, or active-pointer authority.
The runtime may manage only an exact registry entry and must reject discovery, traversal, symlinks, and undeclared reads.
Unrelated bytes outside a selected definition section are diagnostic, while changed selected bytes block the snapshot.
A runtime wrapper must preserve a native validator PASS, BLOCK, or failure and may never upgrade it.
Cataloging, snapshotting, retrieving, validating, drift observation, and candidate construction create evidence only and never transfer meaning or decision authority.
An admitted epoch and its expected identities are never rewritten; any byte change must produce a distinct successor candidate.
Candidate identity is derived deterministically from canonical manifest content and exact captured bytes, so the same inputs yield the same epoch identity.
A candidate becomes visible only after all files and its manifest are durable and an atomic publication step completes; partial candidates remain non-addressable residue.
A valid candidate cannot update the active registration; an exact owner decision over its immutable identity is a separate prerequisite.
